11. Integration

From the Riemann integral to the Lebesgue integral — how the idea of integration expands.

  • The Gamma Function — The factorial stretched to real arguments — Γ(x+1)=xΓ(x)\Gamma(x+1) = x\Gamma(x)Γ(x+1)=xΓ(x), so Γ(n+1)=n!\Gamma(n+1) = n!Γ(n+1)=n!. Watch the improper integral converge for x>0x > 0x>0.
  • The Beta Function — The area under \t^{p-1}(1-t)^{q-1}\ is the beta function — morph its shape with the \p\, \q\ sliders. Also covers \B(p,q) = \\Gamma(p)\\Gamma(q)/\\Gamma(p+q)\, the bridge to the gamma function.
  • Bohr–Mollerup Theorem — f(1)=1f(1) = 1f(1)=1 and f(x+1)=x f(x)f(x+1) = x\,f(x)f(x+1)=xf(x) do not pin down the continuous extension of the factorial — the impostor Γ(x)(1+asin⁡2πx)\Gamma(x)(1 + a\sin 2\pi x)Γ(x)(1+asin2πx) matches Γ\GammaΓ at every integer and survives. Watch the secant test expose log-convexity as Γ\GammaΓ's true fingerprint.
  • Improper Integrals — ∫1∞dxxp\int_1^\infty \frac{dx}{x^p}∫1∞​xpdx​ converges only for p>1p > 1p>1, plus the singular kind ∫01dxx=2\int_0^1 \frac{dx}{\sqrt{x}} = 2∫01​x​dx​=2 — the twin of the p-series scene.
  • Gabriel's Horn — Rotating y=1/xy = 1/xy=1/x (x≥1x \ge 1x≥1) makes a horn with finite volume π\piπ but infinite surface area — fillable with π\piπ of paint, yet unpaintable. The painter's paradox.
  • Upper and Lower Sums Close In — Fill rectangles under f(x)=x2f(x) = x^2f(x)=x2. The lower and upper sums squeeze 13\frac{1}{3}31​ from both sides.
  • The Dirichlet Function — 1Q\mathbf{1}_{\mathbb{Q}}1Q​ is 1 on the rationals and 0 on the irrationals of [0,1][0, 1][0,1] — every subinterval holds both, so the upper sum is always 1 and the lower sum always 0. The canonical non-Riemann-integrable function: no refinement closes the gap.
  • Volterra's Function — Differentiable everywhere with a bounded derivative — yet the derivative is not Riemann integrable. A sum of (x−a)2(b−x)2sin⁡1x−a(x-a)^2(b-x)^2\sin\frac{1}{x-a}(x−a)2(b−x)2sinx−a1​-type bumps over a fat Cantor set builds this legendary counterexample.
  • The Area Function's Derivative Is the Function — Measure the slope of the area function A(x)=∫axf(t) dtA(x) = \int_a^x f(t)\,dtA(x)=∫ax​f(t)dt — it equals f(x)f(x)f(x). Drag xxx.
  • Integration by Parts — Integrate the product rule and get ∫u dv=[uv]−∫v du\int u\,dv = [uv] - \int v\,du∫udv=[uv]−∫vdu — split the area into two pieces and compute each. Move bbb: both sides agree to the last decimal.
  • Change of Variables — Stretch and squeeze the axis with u=φ(x)u = \varphi(x)u=φ(x) and the limits follow — ∫abf(φ)φ′=∫φ(a)φ(b)f\int_a^b f(\varphi)\varphi' = \int_{\varphi(a)}^{\varphi(b)} f∫ab​f(φ)φ′=∫φ(a)φ(b)​f. Watch two substitutions collapse onto the same integral.
  • Functions of Bounded Variation — A function has bounded variation when ∑∣f(xi)−f(xi−1)∣\sum \lvert f(x_i) - f(x_{i-1})\rvert∑∣f(xi​)−f(xi−1​)∣ stays under a finite ceiling as partitions refine — every monotone function qualifies, while xsin⁡(1/x)x\sin(1/x)xsin(1/x), wiggling endlessly near 0, does not.
  • The Riemann–Stieltjes Integral — Changing the integrator — ∫abf dα\int_a^b f\,d\alpha∫ab​fdα weighs intervals by Δαi=α(xi)−α(xi−1)\Delta\alpha_i = \alpha(x_i) - \alpha(x_{i-1})Δαi​=α(xi​)−α(xi−1​) instead of length. α(x)=x\alpha(x) = xα(x)=x recovers Riemann sums, a step α\alphaα collapses to a single jump, α(x)=x2\alpha(x) = x^2α(x)=x2 gives ∫fα′ dx\int f\alpha'\,dx∫fα′dx.
  • Jordan Decomposition — Every BV function is a difference of two increasing functions — f=g−hf = g - hf=g−h with g(x)=V0x(f)g(x) = V_0^x(f)g(x)=V0x​(f) the variation function. Drag the probe point over x2sin⁡1xx^2\sin\frac{1}{x}x2sinx1​ and watch the identity hold pointwise.
  • Lebesgue Measure — Outer measure is the cheapest countable interval cover of a set. A single point — and even all the rationals — cost nothing. Measurable sets and countable additivity need the Carathéodory construction (idea level only).
  • The Vitali Set — Using the axiom of choice to pick one representative from each class of R/Q\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Q}R/Q births a non-measurable set. Countably many disjoint translates cover [0,1][0,1][0,1] inside [−1,2][-1,2][−1,2] — yet measure 0 gives total 0 and positive measure gives infinity. Both impossible.
  • Borel–Cantelli Lemmas — If the total length is finite, the points hit infinitely often form a null set — ∑m(En)<∞⇒m(lim sup⁡En)=0\sum m(E_n) < \infty \Rightarrow m(\limsup E_n) = 0∑m(En​)<∞⇒m(limsupEn​)=0. With independence the converse holds.
  • Covering the Rationals with Nothing — Cover the rationals one by one with ε/2k\varepsilon/2^kε/2k covers — the total length drops below ε\varepsilonε. Riemann can't move.
  • Lebesgue Convergence Theorems — Monotone convergence, Fatou, dominated convergence — the three pillars for swapping limits and integrals. Watch mass escape (escape·spike) to see why each hypothesis is needed.
  • Fubini–Tonelli Theorem — Nonnegative (Tonelli) or integrable (Fubini) functions give the same iterated integrals in either order — rows-first or columns-first. Without integrability it breaks.
  • Egorov's Theorem — On finite measure, a.e. convergence is "almost" uniform — squeeze the bad set's measure below ε\varepsilonε and convergence is uniform on the rest.
  • Absolute Continuity — F(x)=x2F(x) = x^2F(x)=x2 is absolutely continuous — when the intervals' total length goes to 0, so does ∑∣ΔF∣\sum |\Delta F|∑∣ΔF∣. The Cantor function is uniformly continuous but not absolutely continuous: total length (23)n→0\left(\frac23\right)^n \to 0(32​)n→0 while ∑∣Δc∣=1\sum |\Delta c| = 1∑∣Δc∣=1 stays frozen. Absolutely continuous functions are exactly the indefinite integrals of Lebesgue-integrable functions.
